title: Jacobi.Midi exchange file
description: The message exchange patterns of one map root (see readme.md). The same content as the XML format (exchange.xsd): elements that repeat are arrays. Not expressed here, checked by the reader: 'goto' names a turn of the same exchange, every turn can be reached from the first one, 'sent' needs a 'send' in the turn, 'received' a 'receive', 'retry' is only for 'timeout' and messages, and names of exchanges and turns are unique, ignoring case. Defaults, for a turn without an 'on' for the event: 'received' (a turn with a 'receive') and 'sent' (a turn with a 'send' that waits for nothing: no 'receive' and no 'on') give the result 'completed', 'timeout' gives 'timedOut'.

for.description: The schema name of the map root whose ranges these exchanges transfer, e.g. 'Gx700.AddressMap'.

responseTimeout.description: Milliseconds a turn waits for an event; default 1000 (an exchange takes the file's value).

messageInterval.description: The least number of milliseconds between two messages sent to the device; default 0 (an exchange takes the file's value).

messageName.description: The schema name of a message group: document, root and path, e.g. 'Roland.Message32.RQ1'.

exchange.description: One exchange: a state machine of turns that runs once per block of the range; the first turn is the start.

name.description: A standard name (requestData, sendData) or a name of the file's own.

turn.description: A turn in the conversation with the device: on entry it sends its message (if any), then waits for the events it has an 'on' for (or a default: see the description of the file).

send.description: The message to build for the block and send on entry.

receive.description: The data messages whose data is accepted for the block while in the turn, and counts towards 'received'.

on.description: The transitions; the first one that matches is taken.

transition.description: On the event or message: enter the turn again while retries are left, then go to a turn, or end the run for the block with a result.

retry.description: The most times the turn is entered again (its message sent again) for this 'on', per block; then its 'goto' or 'result' is taken.
